summary.text: Define integers \(u_0=1,u_1=-2\) by \(u_{n+2}=-4u_{n+1}-64u_n\); eliminating the cross term \(u_{n+2}u_{n+1}\) shows that \(u_{n+1}^2\) and the odd-indexed subsequence obey the same third-order recurrence \(x_{n+3}=-48x_{n+2}+3072x_{n+1}+262144x_n\). They agree in their first three values, so induction gives \(a(2n+1)=u_{n+1}^2\) for every \(n\).

full_proof.text:
Let \((a_n)_{n\ge 0}\) be the integer sequence defined by
\[
a_0=-1,\qquad a_1=4,\qquad a_2=176,\qquad a_3=3136,
\]
and, for every \(r\ge 0\),
\[
a_{r+4}=-4a_{r+3}+256a_{r+1}+4096a_r. \tag{1}
\]
We prove that every odd-indexed term \(a_{2n+1}\) is a perfect square.

Define an auxiliary integer sequence \((u_n)_{n\ge 0}\) by
\[
u_0=1,\qquad u_1=-2,
\]
and
\[
u_{n+2}=-4u_{n+1}-64u_n\qquad(n\ge 0). \tag{2}
\]
We will prove the stronger identity
\[
a_{2n+1}=u_{n+1}^2 \qquad(n\ge 0). \tag{3}
\]
The desired assertion follows immediately from (3).

First, we derive a recurrence for the odd-indexed terms of \(a\). Applying (1) at three consecutive relevant positions gives, for every \(n\ge 0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{2n+7}&=-4a_{2n+6}+256a_{2n+4}+4096a_{2n+3}, \tag{4}\\
a_{2n+6}&=-4a_{2n+5}+256a_{2n+3}+4096a_{2n+2}, \tag{5}\\
a_{2n+5}&=-4a_{2n+4}+256a_{2n+2}+4096a_{2n+1}. \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitute (5) into (4). This yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{2n+7}
&=-4\bigl(-4a_{2n+5}+256a_{2n+3}+4096a_{2n+2}\bigr)
  +256a_{2n+4}+4096a_{2n+3}\\
&=16a_{2n+5}+3072a_{2n+3}-16384a_{2n+2}+256a_{2n+4}. \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, multiplying (6) by \(-64\) gives
\[
-64a_{2n+5}=256a_{2n+4}-16384a_{2n+2}-262144a_{2n+1},
\]
so
\[
256a_{2n+4}-16384a_{2n+2}
=-64a_{2n+5}+262144a_{2n+1}. \tag{8}
\]
Using (8) in (7), we obtain
\[
a_{2n+7}=-48a_{2n+5}+3072a_{2n+3}+262144a_{2n+1}. \tag{9}
\]
Thus, if we set
\[
b_n:=a_{2n+1},
\]
then (9) says
\[
b_{n+3}=-48b_{n+2}+3072b_{n+1}+262144b_n
\qquad(n\ge 0). \tag{10}
\]

We next show that the squares \(u_{n+1}^2\) satisfy exactly the same third-order recurrence. Define
\[
w_n:=u_{n+1}^2,
\qquad
z_n:=u_{n+2}u_{n+1}.
\]
The mixed product \(z_n\) is introduced so that squaring the second-order recurrence (2) can be handled without losing its cross term.

From (2),
\[
u_{n+3}=-4u_{n+2}-64u_{n+1}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
z_{n+1}
&=u_{n+3}u_{n+2}\\
&=(-4u_{n+2}-64u_{n+1})u_{n+2}\\
&=-4u_{n+2}^2-64u_{n+2}u_{n+1}\\
&=-4w_{n+1}-64z_n. \tag{11}
\end{aligned}
\]
Similarly, squaring the same recurrence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{n+2}
&=u_{n+3}^2\\
&=(-4u_{n+2}-64u_{n+1})^2\\
&=16u_{n+2}^2+512u_{n+2}u_{n+1}+4096u_{n+1}^2\\
&=16w_{n+1}+512z_n+4096w_n. \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
Apply (12) with \(n+1\) in place of \(n\), and then use (11):
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{n+3}
&=16w_{n+2}+512z_{n+1}+4096w_{n+1}\\
&=16w_{n+2}+512(-4w_{n+1}-64z_n)+4096w_{n+1}\\
&=16w_{n+2}+2048w_{n+1}-32768z_n. \tag{13}
\end{aligned}
\]
Equation (12) can also be rewritten as
\[
512z_n=w_{n+2}-16w_{n+1}-4096w_n.
\]
Therefore
\[
-32768z_n=-64w_{n+2}+1024w_{n+1}+262144w_n. \tag{14}
\]
Substituting (14) into (13), we find
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{n+3}
&=16w_{n+2}+2048w_{n+1}
  -64w_{n+2}+1024w_{n+1}+262144w_n\\
&=-48w_{n+2}+3072w_{n+1}+262144w_n. \tag{15}
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \((w_n)\) satisfies exactly the same recurrence as \((b_n)\).

It remains to check the three initial values required by this third-order recurrence. From (2),
\[
u_2=-4u_1-64u_0=-4(-2)-64(1)=-56,
\]
and
\[
u_3=-4u_2-64u_1=-4(-56)-64(-2)=224+128=352.
\]
Hence
\[
w_0=u_1^2=(-2)^2=4,
\]
\[
w_1=u_2^2=(-56)^2=3136,
\]
and
\[
w_2=u_3^2=352^2=123904. \tag{16}
\]

For the corresponding odd-indexed terms of \(a\), the first two are initial values:
\[
b_0=a_1=4,
\qquad
b_1=a_3=3136.
\]
To calculate \(b_2=a_5\), first use (1) at \(r=0\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_4
&=-4a_3+256a_1+4096a_0\\
&=-4(3136)+256(4)+4096(-1)\\
&=-12544+1024-4096\\
&=-15616.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then use (1) at \(r=1\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_5
&=-4a_4+256a_2+4096a_1\\
&=-4(-15616)+256(176)+4096(4)\\
&=62464+45056+16384\\
&=123904.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
b_0=w_0,
\qquad b_1=w_1,
\qquad b_2=w_2. \tag{17}
\]

We now prove \(b_n=w_n\) for every \(n\ge 0\) by induction. Equality holds for \(n=0,1,2\) by (17). Suppose for some \(n\ge 0\) that
\[
b_n=w_n,\qquad b_{n+1}=w_{n+1},\qquad b_{n+2}=w_{n+2}.
\]
Using the common recurrences (10) and (15),
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_{n+3}
&=-48b_{n+2}+3072b_{n+1}+262144b_n\\
&=-48w_{n+2}+3072w_{n+1}+262144w_n\\
&=w_{n+3}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the equality propagates from each three-term window to the next, proving it for all \(n\).

Finally, by the definitions of \(b_n\) and \(w_n\), this equality is precisely
\[
a_{2n+1}=b_n=w_n=u_{n+1}^2.
\]
Since \(u_{n+1}\) is an integer, this exhibits \(a_{2n+1}\) as an integer square for every nonnegative integer \(n\). Hence every odd-indexed term of A113254 is a perfect square.
